title: Senior asks: a user with a German Excel saves fruits.csv with semicolons: id;fruit. The reader splits on commas. What does this print?
explain: The default delimiter is a comma. The line has no comma, so it is one single column named id;fruit. The next check (column count or unique headers) then fails in a confusing way. Good fix: a clear 422 message such as 'CSV must use commas', or detect the delimiter on purpose.

title: composer.json has "vendor/tool": "^0.3.1". Which versions can composer update install?
explain: The caret allows changes that do not touch the left-most non-zero part. For ^1.2.3 that is <2.0.0. For ^0.3.1 the left-most non-zero part is the 3, so the limit is <0.4.0. Versions 0.x are seen as unstable: a minor step can break things, so the caret is tighter there.

title: What does Node print?
explain: this is set by how a function is called, not where it is written. user.hi() uses user as this, so this.name is 'Ola'. f.call({ name: 5 }) sets this by hand, so this.name is 5. A method taken out of its object loses its this unless you bind it or use call/apply.
